# Appearance

## Existence

```
Grounded ( Ground )

Properties ( Thing )

Thing ( Matters )

Matters ( Form ) ⟹ Existing-Essence

Form ( Matters ) ⟹ Form ( Content )

Existing-Essence ⧁ Form ( Content )

Existing-Essence ⧁ Appearance
```

Existence is a for-itself concept that subsumes Essence, Shine and their relationship of Ground. What exists are Things, reflects itself through its Ground. 

If we determine the Thing as Grounded, then the Ground for the Thing are its Properties. 

However, if we determine the Thing as Ground, then what is Grounded in the Thing are its Matters.



## Appearance

```
Existing-Essence ⧁ Appearance

Existing-Essence ⧁ Appearance ( Law of Appearance )

Existing-Essence ⧁ Appearance ( Form ⇄ Content )

Existing-Essence ⧁ Appearance ( Form ⇄ ~~Content~~ ) ⟹ External Form

Existing-Essence ⧁ Appearance ( ~~Form~~ ⇄ Content ) ⟹ External Content

Existing-Essence | ~~Appearance~~ ( Form-Content )

Existing-Essence ⟹ Whole

Form-Content ⟹ Parts
```



## Essential Relation

```
Whole ⧁ Parts 
```

The Whole was previously the Existing-Essence (Erscheinende) because it is the thought or identity of concept as a whole and the Parts were the Matters that were left behind when Appearance disappeared because each Matter had its own Form and Content that could not be reduced to one Appearance.

Take a watch for example — the balance spring would not be what it is without the watch. The whole watch gives all its parts content because the parts are necessary for the whole watch to be what it is and the whole watch implies the form and content of each of its parts. The different parts of watch as a whole can only be organized in such a way (form) such that their structure in which they are organized implies their different functions (content) that in turn logically implies the whole concept of what a watch is. 

```
Whole ⧁ Parts ⟹ Force

Whole ⧀ Parts ⟹ Expression

Force ⧁ Expression
```

Force is the presentation of the Whole reflected in the totality of its Parts, which are shown to be the Expression of the Force. Equivalently stated, the Force is the Identity of the Whole and Parts and Expression is the Difference of the Whole and Parts.


```
Force ⧁ Expression ⟹ Inner

Force ⧀ Expression ⟹ Outer

Inner ⟲ Outer 
```
